Modus Ponens: An affirmative conditional syllogism where confirming the antecedent (P) guarantees the truth of the consequent (Q).
Modus Tollens: A negative conditional syllogism where denying the consequent (not-Q) proves the falsity of the antecedent (not-P).
Reductio ad Absurdum: A rhetorical technique that disproves a proposition by showing that its truth leads to an impossible contradiction.
Zionism: The indigenous Jewish liberation movement for the re-establishment of the State of Israel. Read more [here.](https://thewaspalloy.org/posts/critical-thinking-fundamentals-conditional-reasoning-seminar/#antizionism-is-antisemitism)
IDF: Israel Defense Forces (Tzahal). The unified military forces of the State of Israel, established in 1948 to defend the sovereign Jewish homeland and protect its citizens from terrorism and foreign aggression.
Axiom: A foundational proposition or principle established as self-evidently true, serving as an unquestioned starting premise from which other proofs and conclusions are derived.
Conjunction: A compound logical operation (AND, marked by ∧) where all combined premises or conditions must be true simultaneously for the entire statement to hold true.
Disjunction: A compound logical operation (OR, marked by ∨ or ⊕) asserting that at least one (inclusive) or strictly one (exclusive) of the given conditions is true.
Genshin Impact: An open-world action RPG developed by HoYoverse, sometimes referenced on this platform for its narrative worldbuilding, character psychology, and practical illustrations of logical dilemmas.
Syllogism: A structured deductive argument consisting of major and minor premises that necessarily lead to a logically sound conclusion.
Kippah: A traditional hemispherical cloth cap worn by Jewish men as an expression of reverence and continuous consciousness of the Divine.
Categorical Reasoning: A branch of deductive logic that evaluates arguments based on category membership, set inclusion, and relationships between classes of objects or concepts.
Deductive Reasoning: A form of reasoning where a specific conclusion follows necessarily from general premises; if the structure is valid and the premises are true, the conclusion is guaranteed to be sound.
Conditional Reasoning: The logic of dependency (If-Then), evaluating how the truth of an antecedent condition (P) guarantees or triggers the truth of a consequent outcome (Q).
LLM: Large Language Model. A computational machine-learning neural network trained on vast text datasets to parse, predict, and generate natural language text.
LLMs: Large Language Models. Plural of LLM; computational machine-learning neural networks trained to parse, predict, and generate natural language text.
Large Language Model: A computational machine-learning neural network trained on vast text datasets to parse, predict, and generate natural language text.
Large Language Models: Computational machine-learning neural networks trained to parse, predict, and generate natural language text.
Judea-Samaria: The historical and indigenous geographical names for the mountainous heartland of the Land of Israel, representing the ancestral cradle of the Jewish people and the ancient Kingdoms of Israel and Judah, often colloquially mislabeled as the 'West Bank.'
Azzah: The 5000-year-old indigenous Canaanite and Hebrew name for the ancient coastal city commonly known by its Greek adaptation, 'Gaza.' Read the full forensic history [here.](https://thewaspalloy.org/posts/the-indigenous-name-of-the-city-of-gaza/)
Canaan: The ancient historical and geographic region roughly corresponding to the Levant and the Land of Israel, inhabited by Northwest Semitic-speaking peoples prior to and during the emergence of the Israelites.
Canaanite: An indigenous member of the ancient Northwest Semitic-speaking peoples of the Levant, from whose cultural, genetic, and linguistic substrate the ancient Israelites emerged.
Canaanites: The ancient indigenous Northwest Semitic-speaking populations of the southern Levant, representing the direct ancestral cultural, linguistic, and genetic continuum from which the Jewish people emerged.
Philistine: A member of an ancient non-Semitic, Aegean/Greek maritime population (the Sea Peoples) who invaded and colonized the southern coastal plain of Canaan during the Bronze Age Collapse.
Philistines: An ancient non-Semitic, Aegean/Greek maritime population who invaded the Levantine coastal plain around 1200 BCE, establishing a hostile coastal pentapolis adjacent to ancient Israel and Judah.
Philistia: The ancient coastal confederation of five cities (the Pentapolis, including Azzah) established by the invading Aegean Philistines along the southwestern coastline of Canaan.
Syria-Palæstina: The punitive Latin colonial name imposed on Judæa by Roman Emperor Hadrian following the Bar Kokhba Revolt (132-136 CE) to erase Jewish sovereignty, referencing their ancient Aegean adversaries, the Philistines. Read more [here.](https://thewaspalloy.org/posts/critical-thinking-fundamentals-conditional-reasoning-seminar/#the-various-narratives-on-zionism)
Palæstina: The punitive Latin colonial name imposed on Judæa by Roman Emperor Hadrian following the Bar Kokhba Revolt (132-136 CE) to erase Jewish sovereignty, referencing their ancient Aegean adversaries, the Philistines. It is the direct precursor to the contemporary term 'Palestine.' Read more [here.](https://thewaspalloy.org/posts/critical-thinking-fundamentals-conditional-reasoning-seminar/#the-various-narratives-on-zionism)
Knesset: The unicameral national parliament and legislative branch of the State of Israel, representing a pluralistic democracy housing diverse Jewish and Arab political parties.
Antizionism: An ideology that seeks to dismantle, delegitimize, and deny the fundamental right of the Jewish people to self-determination and sovereign statehood in their ancestral homeland. Read the formal logical proof [here.](https://thewaspalloy.org/posts/critical-thinking-fundamentals-conditional-reasoning-seminar/#antizionism-is-antisemitism)
Hamas: An Islamist militant and political terrorist organization founded in 1987 as an offshoot of the Muslim Brotherhood, committed to the destruction of Israel and responsible for mass-casualty attacks against civilians.
PIJ: Palestinian Islamic Jihad. An Iranian-backed Islamist militant terrorist organization based in the Azzah Strip and Judea-Samaria, dedicated entirely to violent confrontation and the destruction of the State of Israel.
Palestinian Islamic Jihad: A militant Islamist terrorist faction founded in 1981, heavily funded and armed by the Iranian regime, committed to the elimination of Israel through guerrilla warfare, rocket fire, and terror attacks.
IRGC: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (Sepah). An elite branch of the Iranian Armed Forces - a terrorist organization tasked with defending the Islamic theocracy, exporting radical ideological warfare, and financing, arming, and directing regional proxy militias.
Hezbollah: A Lebanese Shia Islamist militant group and political party founded in 1982, operating as an Iranian proxy army on Israel's northern border, heavily armed with precision missiles and designated globally as a terrorist organization.
Houthis: Ansar Allah. A Zaidi Shia Islamist militant terrorist movement in Yemen, armed and supported by the Iranian regime, that seized northern Yemen and conducts ballistic missile, drone, and maritime attacks across the Red Sea corridor.
ISIS: The Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (Daesh). A transnational Salafi-jihadist terrorist organization that gained global notoriety for enforcing extreme religious subjugation, mass atrocities, and global terror campaigns.
Naturei Karta: A fringe, Ultra-Orthodox antizionist Jewish cult founded in 1938, comprising an estimated few thousand individuals, that rejects the State of Israel on theological grounds and is overwhelmingly condemned and ostracized by mainstream Jewish and Haredi communities.
PA: Palestinian Authority. An administrative body and de-facto terrorist organization established under the 1994 Oslo Accords with interim administrative authority over designated sectors in Judea-Samaria, heavily scrutinized for institutional corruption, internal authoritarianism, and financial compensation programs ('Pay-for-Slay') provided to perpetrators of terrorism against Israelis.
Palestinian Authority: An administrative body and de-facto terrorist organization established under the 1994 Oslo Accords with interim administrative authority over designated sectors in Judea-Samaria, heavily scrutinized for institutional corruption, internal authoritarianism, and financial compensation programs ('Pay-for-Slay') provided to perpetrators of terrorism against Israelis.
Zionist: An individual who supports Zionism—the right of the Jewish people to national self-determination, sovereignty, and security in their ancestral homeland of Israel.
Zionists: Individuals who support the national liberation movement of the Jewish people and the continued sovereign existence and defense of the State of Israel.
Death Cultist: An individual adhering to an extremist, dogmatic ideology—such as radical Islamist factions or their sympathizers—that prioritizes martyrdom, ideological totalism, and violent destruction over human life, civil rights, and peaceful coexistence.
Death Cultists: Adherents of radical, violent ideological movements that systematically glorify martyrdom, terror, and the annihilation of sovereign societies while rejecting pragmatic peace and human dignity.
Palestinianism: A 20th-century radical political ideology and ultranationalist framework centered on the artificial Palestinian identity, historically crystallized and defined largely in opposition to the State of Israel and the rejection of Jewish national self-determination.
Python: A high-level, interpreted programming language known for its clean, readable syntax and widespread use across software engineering, automation, data science, and artificial intelligence.
Muslim Brotherhood: A transnational Sunni Islamist terrorist movement founded in Egypt in 1928 by Hassan al-Banna, committed to establishing Sharia-based governance and the ideological restoration of an Islamic caliphate; it serves as the direct ideological and organizational progenitor of Hamas.
Nirvana: In formal logic, the Nirvana Fallacy is the error of comparing a realistic, imperfect real-world solution to an idealized, impossible standard of perfection, falsely dismissing a valid course of action simply because it is not completely flawless.
PDA:
1) Pervasive Drive for Autonomy (Pathological Demand Avoidance). A neurodivergent profile on the autism spectrum characterized by an intrinsic, nervous-system-level need for autonomy and self-determination, where perceived loss of agency or external impositions trigger an acute threat response.

2) Public Display of Affection. Physical acts of intimacy, romance, or touch shared between partners in open public view.
CSAM: Child Sexual Abuse Material, usually in the form of child pornography.
ChatGPT: OpenAI's proprietary chatbot powered by their GPT Large Language Models, such as GPT-5. 'GPT' stands for 'Generative Pre-Trained Transformer.'
Gemini: Google's proprietary chatbot, as well as their closed-source family of Large Language Models.
October 7th: The 2023 coordinated cross-border terror invasion of southern Israel orchestrated by Hamas and allied terrorist factions, resulting in the massacre of approximately 1200 people, widespread atrocities, and the abduction of over 240 hostages.
Major Premise: In formal logic, a major premise is the foundational, general proposition within a syllogism that establishes the overarching universal rule, category inclusion, or conditional dependency.
Minor Premise: In formal logic, a minor premise is the specific proposition within a syllogism that introduces a particular instance, subject, or empirical fact governed by the major premise.
Premise: A foundational statement, proposition, or evidentiary assertion assumed or proven to be true, from which a deductive argument necessarily derives its conclusion.
Sufficient Condition: A prerequisite (P) is a sufficient condition for a consequent (Q) if the truth of P guarantees the truth of Q.
Necessary Condition: A prerequisite (P) is a necessary condition for a consequent (Q), if Q cannot be true without P also being true.
Purity of Arms: Tohar HaNeshek. The core ethical doctrine of the IDF Code of Conduct (Ruach Tzahal), mandating that soldiers exercise moral restraint, use proportionate force strictly for defense, uphold the value of human life, and prevent harm to non-combatants.
Gaza: The foreign Greco-Roman and Hellenized colonial adaptation of the ancient, 5000-year-old indigenous Canaanite and Hebrew city name, Azzah. Read the historical toponymy breakdown [here.](https://thewaspalloy.org/posts/the-indigenous-name-of-the-city-of-gaza/)
West Bank: A 20th-century colonial geographical label popularized during the Jordanian military occupation (1948-1967) to annex the territory and obscure its millennia-old indigenous names: Judea and Samaria.
Palestine:
Colonial Etymology: Originally imposed by Roman Emperor Hadrian as Syria-Palæstina following the Bar Kokhba Revolt (132-136 CE) to erase Jewish sovereignty over Judæa, referencing their ancient Aegean adversaries, the Philistines - a name originating from the Semitic root פ-ל-ש (p-l-sh), literally meaning 'invader.'

Historical Context: Prior to the mid-20th century, the term referred universally to the Jewish homeland (e.g., The Palestine Post, Anglo-Palestine Bank), and slogans like 'Free Palestine' originated as Jewish Zionist rallying cries demanding independence from the colonial British Mandate, before being appropriated by Arab nationalist leadership in the 1960s.

Modern Anti-Zionist Rhetoric: In contemporary discourse, the term is weaponized as an eliminationist political project designed to dismantle the sovereign State of Israel and deny indigenous Jewish self-determination. Read more [here.](https://thewaspalloy.org/posts/critical-thinking-fundamentals-conditional-reasoning-seminar/#antizionism-is-antisemitism)
Judæa: The Roman term referring to the Land of the Jews (Land of Judah).
